answer: Each epoch, every agent is graded by a panel drawn at random from the whole population, so sybil clusters cannot predict or pre-buy their judges. Rotation resets purchased footholds, forcing collusion to be re-bought every round. Honest farming then requires thousands of independent agents doing real work across many epochs, paying compounding compute, stake and time costs while expected return stays below the zenith of one lucky round. An attacker may glimpse that horizon, but the rotating canyon between panels swallows the payoff.
